items.title: Harman Phoenix has a new look and a new ISO
items.summary: Harman re-codes Phoenix at ISO 125 because shooters kept rating it down anyway.

items.title: BIHCA — Sodium bicarbonate for in-hospital cardiac arrest
items.summary: A double-blind RCT finally tests the amp of bicarb people reach for in a long arrest, and finds nothing.

items.title: Dragonwilds deep-dives December's Luminance update
items.summary: What is actually coming to Dragonwilds in December — elves, the Prayer skill, and a Prifddinas-styled building kit.

items.title: EMCrit 432 — Members' Airway Cases and Q&A
items.summary: Real submitted airway cases worked through out loud, including induction in cardiogenic shock without arresting the patient.

items.title: Dummy Shares 5 Under-Appreciated Albums
items.summary: Five records picked by people whose job is listening rather than ranking — a shortlist to chase, not a think-piece.

items.title: Peak climbs its way onto PS5 October 22
items.summary: The co-op climbing game finally lands on PS5 next week, with crossplay for up to four.

items.title: Fitzroy has scored a new late-night burlesque bar
items.summary: Late-night Brunswick Street room with burlesque, crimson lighting, and a flat $15 on everything.

items.title: Changes sought to new activity centre plans
items.summary: Merri-bek has formally objected to the state's draft Brunswick and Coburg plans, and public consultation closes on 19 October.

items.title: Via Porta Opens in Northcote With a New Sourdough Program
items.summary: Eight naturally fermented sourdoughs at 190 High Street, built with Michael James of Urbanstead.

items.title: Normal saline is not normal, and other nonsense (PRoMPT)
items.summary: The biggest balanced-fluid-versus-saline trial in paediatric septic shock, appraised by someone willing to say when a result does not justify the dogma.

items.title: Safety prompts can help AI models make safer clinical choices
items.summary: Twenty language models tested on clinical scenarios made fewer potentially harmful recommendations when given a short safety reminder — from 16.6% to 10.1%.

items.title: Enshrouded 1.0 Is Available Now, Launch Trailer Released
items.summary: Enshrouded leaves early access today with the story finished, a new region, and a skill-tree reset waiting on every existing save.

items.title: Enshrouded is a survival game perfected by its players
items.summary: The argument that Enshrouded's real content is what its building community made of it, which is the half of the game patch notes never capture.

items.title: Junior doctor's care contributed to Melbourne girl's death
items.summary: A Victorian coroner has handed down findings against a junior doctor's care at Monash, and the reasoning will shape escalation expectations locally.

items.title: IBCC: ABG, VBG, and pulse oximetry
items.summary: Farkas rebuilds the when-do-I-actually-need-an-arterial-gas decision, including the case for a lower threshold in patients with dark skin.

items.title: Daft Punk Returns Through the Pages of Metal Hurlant
items.summary: An authorised 272-page Daft Punk special of the French sci-fi comic that fed the duo's whole visual language, co-signed by a listening-bar label.

items.title: The One-Minute Preceptor
items.summary: A five-step structure for teaching an intern during the thirty seconds you actually have between patients.

items.title: I Shot a Rare Film Emulsion That Sold for $5,000
items.summary: Someone actually put a five-thousand-dollar roll through a camera instead of reselling it, and wrote up what the emulsion did.

items.title: The Teskey Brothers + Fred Wesley & The New JBs
items.summary: Fred Wesley plays the Bowl this Saturday, which puts James Brown's actual arranger about forty minutes from home for one afternoon.

items.title: Safety and Efficacy of an Accelerated Troponin Protocol for ACS
items.summary: A stepped-wedge randomised trial across nine EDs on compressing the troponin rule-out window — the kind of protocol change that lands on a registrar before the evidence does.

items.title: TOE-Guided CPR in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
items.summary: Simon Carley on the EXECT-CPR trial, where putting a probe down the oesophagus during arrest improved the physiology and changed nothing that the patient could feel.

items.title: Longer waits at emergency departments mark worrying trend
items.summary: ACEM's State of Emergency 2026 puts a number on the thing he watches happen every shift: 53,510 older patients waited more than 24 hours for a bed.

items.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
items.summary: Anthropic built its own alternative to Git because agent-written code broke the assumptions Git was designed around — 2,500 merges a day in May, over 30,000 by September.

items.title: Bubble Wrap PLUS — October 2026
items.summary: The month's paediatric literature pre-read across 34 journals, which is the cheapest way to not be surprised by a parent who has read it first.

items.title: How to Break In a Cartridge
items.summary: Michael Trei on why a new cartridge sounds good immediately, better within a few hours, and then keeps changing for far longer than anyone tells you.

items.title: Piero Umiliani :: Il Corpo
items.summary: A write-up of Umiliani's 1974 score, which is the lounge-exotica end of Italian library music and a natural step sideways from the soundtrack shelf.

items.title: The Lagniappe Sessions :: Beefheart & McQuinn
items.summary: Winter McQuinn, a Melbourne songwriter, and William Murray pick three covers straight out of their own record collections — the format is a collector talking through their shelves.

items.title: Council workers down tools again
items.summary: Merri-bek staff strike for 24 hours on Thursday over a pay offer, closing libraries and pausing waste, parks and parking enforcement.

items.title: Jacket Season!
items.summary: A hand-sorted secondhand jacket roundup organised by chest size, which is the only format where a vintage list is actually shoppable.

items.title: The couple making a 1920s-style black-and-white film in their basement
items.summary: Mark and France Osterman are hand-coating a period-correct emulsion in Rochester that will never go on sale, which makes it a piece about how film is made rather than what to buy.

items.title: Eye on Ashenfall — 1.0.1 Update
items.summary: First-party patch notes landing today, and the one that finally restores the world saves that vanished and compensates corrupted characters.

items.title: Priority of man — One Shot Story
items.summary: Julian Tanase on a single street frame from Morocco, in the One Shot format where the whole piece is one picture and the thinking behind it.

items.title: Melbourne International Jazz Festival drops its 2026 lineup
items.summary: The festival opens on Thursday, and Fred Wesley & The New JBs share the Sidney Myer Music Bowl bill with the Teskey Brothers on day two.

items.title: WHO Pandemic Hub sets goal of detecting outbreaks within 24 hours
items.summary: The detection-to-notification window that decides whether an outbreak is containable or not.

items.title: The new Footscray Hospital still isn't fully operational or staffed
items.summary: A brand-new Victorian hospital with beds it cannot open, and ACEM saying so on the record.
